age.evidence: Adult male and female C57BL/6J mice (Jackson Laboratory, Strain #: 000664) were used.

sex.evidence: Adult male and female C57BL/6J mice ... were used. ... both sexes were included in approximately equal numbers unless otherwise noted.

dosing.evidence: Lisuride maleate (Tocris) was used at 0.5 mg/kg ... All drugs were delivered intraperitoneally (i.p.) in sterile saline (0.9%).
LSD (NIDA Drug Supply Program) was used at 0.1 mg/kg, corresponding to peak HTR response ... All drugs were delivered intraperitoneally (i.p.) in sterile saline (0.9%).
For 5HT2AR block, 0.5 mg/kg MDL 100907 (MDL, Tocris) was injected 15 minutes before lisuride or LSD; control animals received two saline injections 15 min apart.

day_night_flipped.evidence: Behavioral and physiological assays were performed during the light phase.

assays.assay_description: HTRs recorded with high-speed video (Basler ACE2) for 30 min immediately after i.p. injection of saline, lisuride (0.5 mg/kg), LSD (0.1 mg/kg) or MDL 100907 + LSD; counts scored post hoc in 5-min bins by a blinded observer.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were delivered intraperitoneally (i.p.) in sterile saline (0.9%).

setup_restrain.evidence: recorded HTRs using high-speed video (Basler ACE2) for 30 min immediately following drug injection; no restraint described

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in recording apparatus during the 30-min HTR recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in recording apparatus during the 30-min HTR recording

time_to_assay.evidence: recorded HTRs using high-speed video (Basler ACE2) for 30 min immediately following drug injection.

sample_size.evidence: n = 3 for all drug conditions for each sex

outcomes.summary: LSD (0.1 mg/kg) evoked a robust HTR in both sexes, peaking ~10 min after injection; lisuride (0.5 mg/kg) did not elicit HTRs. MDL 100907 pretreatment prevented LSD-induced HTRs. No sex differences.
outcomes.evidence: LSD evoked a robust HTR, with peak HTRs occurring 10 minutes after LSD administration, but lisuride did not ... Post-hoc analyses showed that significant increases in head twitch frequency were elicited by LSD in both sexes, but not by saline or LSD+MDL.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Counts were scored post hoc in 5-min bins by a blinded observer (single measure: HTR count)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data is presented in 5-minute bins ... A 2-way repeated measures ANOVA revealed a main effect of time

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is excluded as an ethological behaviour by rubric definition

B5_social.evidence: HTR does not target social behaviour

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR is a drug-induced reflexive response; no learning required

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Counts were scored post hoc in 5-min bins by a blinded observer

D1_continuity.evidence: recorded HTRs ... for 30 min immediately following drug injection

D2_session_duration.evidence: for 30 min immediately following drug injection

D5_followup.evidence: Recording only in the 30 min after injection

assays.assay_description: Locomotor activity in a 44 × 44 × 25 cm arena tracked with EthoVision XT. Mice injected with saline or MDL 100907, explored 30 min, then injected again (saline, lisuride, LSD) and monitored for another 30 min; total distance traveled reported.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were delivered intraperitoneally (i.p.) in sterile saline (0.9%).

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were injected with saline or antagonist, allowed to explore for 30 min, then injected again ... and monitored for another 30 min.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to explore ... open field arena (free-moving apparatus)

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the open field arena

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the open field arena

time_to_assay.evidence: then injected again (saline, lisuride, LSD, or antagonist) and monitored for another 30 min

sample_size.evidence: lisuride (n = 8 females, 8 males); saline (n = 9 females, 8 males); LSD (n = 13 females, 13 males); MDL+lisuride (n = 12 females, 11 males); MDL+LSD (n = 13 females, 13 males); MDL+saline (n = 12 for both females and males)

outcomes.summary: Lisuride (0.5 mg/kg) decreased total distance traveled (~80%) vs saline in both sexes; LSD (0.1 mg/kg) had no effect. MDL pretreatment did not block lisuride hypolocomotion, and MDL+LSD also reduced locomotion vs saline or LSD alone.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA: sex F(1,141) = 4.37, p = 0.04, ηp2 = 0.03; drug F(5,141) = 49.83, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.64; lisuride vs saline p < 0.001; LSD vs saline p = 1; MDL+lisuride vs saline p < 0.001; MDL+LSD vs saline/LSD p < 0.001.
outcomes.evidence: Lisuride significantly decreased distance traveled (n = 8 females, 8 males) compared to saline (n = 9 females, 8 males, p <0.001), as reported previously, whereas LSD had no effect (n = 13 females, 13 males, p = 1).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total distance traveled (m) over 30 min is shown

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total distance traveled (m) over 30 min (single total)

B5_social.evidence: OFT locomotion does not target social behaviour

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Behavioral data was collected using EthoVision XT software (position tracking)

E1_environment_type.evidence: Locomotor activity was assessed in a 44 × 44 × 25 cm arena.

E2_shelter.evidence: open field arena; no shelter described

D4_baseline.evidence: First 30-min exploration followed saline/antagonist injection and its data were not reported; only post-drug total distance shown

assays.assay_description: Accelerating rotarod (3.5 cm diameter, 4–27 rpm over 180 s); after injections (saline/MDL then saline, lisuride or LSD) mice were placed on the rod at various time intervals and latency to fall recorded (max 240 s).

application_type.evidence: All drugs were delivered intraperitoneally (i.p.) in sterile saline (0.9%).

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed on the rod ... latency to fall was recorded

time_to_assay.evidence: After injections, mice were placed on the rod at various time intervals and latency to fall was recorded (specific intervals not stated in text)

sample_size.evidence: All conditions and sexes had five animals, except for MDL+LSD which had only four males.

outcomes.summary: Lisuride (0.5 mg/kg) significantly impaired rotarod performance (reduced latency to fall) in both sexes; LSD (0.1 mg/kg) had no effect. MDL did not block lisuride's impairment (MDL+lisuride even worse than lisuride), and MDL+LSD did not differ from saline.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way RM ANOVA: time F(4,142) = 3.68, p = 0.007; time*sex F(4,128) = 3.23, p = 0.023; time*drug F(20,128) = 4.26, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.316; time*sex*drug F(12,128) = 1.77, p = 0.043; lisuride vs saline p < 0.001; LSD vs saline p = 1; MDL+lisuride vs lisuride p = 0.047; MDL+LSD vs saline p = 0.66.
outcomes.evidence: Lisuride significantly impaired the ability of both females and males to stay on the rod, compared to animals who were injected with saline (p < 0.001). Conversely, LSD had no effect on either sex (p = 1).

B1_num_measures.evidence: latency to fall was recorded (max 240 sec)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Latency measured in separate trials 'at various time intervals' after injection (between-trial comparison, not within-session dynamics)

B5_social.evidence: rotarod does not target social behaviour

B6_cognitive.evidence: Motor coordination was measured on a rotating rod

B7_automated_classification.evidence: latency to fall recorded; no behavioural classifier

D1_continuity.evidence: mice were placed on the rod at various time intervals

D2_session_duration.evidence: latency to fall was recorded (max 240 sec)

D3_recording_days.evidence: After injections, mice were placed on the rod at various time intervals (same day as injection)

assays.assay_description: Two-chamber puzzle box (brightly lit chamber, preferred dark chamber connected by door/tunnel progressively obstructed). Nine trials over 3 days (3/day, 20 min apart); training trials 1-6 on days 1-2; on day 3 saline/MDL then saline, lisuride (trial 7 at 60 min) or LSD (trial 7 at 15 min) before trials 7-9. Latency to enter dark chamber; derived overnight recall (6→7), problem solving (7→8), short-term recall (8→9).

application_type.evidence: All drugs were delivered intraperitoneally (i.p.) in sterile saline (0.9%).

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were trained over two days (trials 1-6) — these are data-collecting training trials, not a separate no-data apparatus habituation

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice moved from a brightly lit chamber to a preferred dark chamber

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the puzzle box

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the puzzle box

time_to_assay.evidence: Based on locomotion data, lisuride groups began trial 7 one-hour post-injection; LSD groups began 15 min after.

sample_size.evidence: lisuride (n = 12 females, 11 males); saline (n = 10 females, 9 males); LSD (n = 8 females, 11 males); MDL followed by LSD (n = 7 females, 7 males); MDL alone (n = 5 females, 5 males); MDL+lisuride n not stated

outcomes.summary: Lisuride (0.5 mg/kg) significantly worsened puzzle box performance (longer latencies) and impaired overnight recall and problem solving; LSD (0.1 mg/kg) had no overall effect and produced a small improvement in short-term recall. MDL did not block lisuride's impairment, while MDL+LSD impaired performance vs saline and LSD alone.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way RM ANOVA: trial F(3,261) = 81.24, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.48; trial*drug F(15,261) = 6.6, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.28; trial*sex F(3,261) = 1.4, p = 0.24; lisuride vs saline p < 0.001; LSD vs saline p = 1; MDL+LSD vs saline p < 0.001, vs LSD p = 0.002. Overnight recall: lisuride vs saline p = 0.012, vs LSD p < 0.001. Problem solving: lisuride vs saline p < 0.001, LSD p = 0.074. Short-term recall: lisuride p = 0.14, LSD p = 0.044.
outcomes.evidence: Contrary to our prediction, lisuride (n = 12 females, 11 males) significantly worsened puzzle box performance compared to saline (n = 10 females, 9 males; p < 0.001), whereas LSD had no significant effect (n = 8 females, 11 males; p = 1).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency to enter the dark chamber; overnight recall (trials 6-7), problem solving (7-8), short-term recall (8-9) reported separately

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Comparisons are across discrete trials, not within a single session

B4_ethological.evidence: Outcome is escape latency, not scored natural behaviours

B5_social.evidence: puzzle box does not involve social behaviour

B6_cognitive.evidence: Identical trials separated by 20 min or 24 h assessed short- and long-term memory, while shifts in barrier configuration assessed problem solving.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Behavioral data was collected using EthoVision XT software (position tracking)

E1_environment_type.evidence: Cognition was tested in a two-chamber puzzle box

E2_shelter.evidence: Mice moved from a brightly lit chamber to a preferred dark chamber

E5_enrichment.evidence: not reported; door/tunnel/barriers are task elements, not enrichment

E6_spatial.evidence: brightly lit and dark chambers of the arena, with the tunnel and door connecting them

D1_continuity.evidence: There are 3 trials each day, separated by 20 min.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Animals that did not complete trials 1-6 within 180 seconds were excluded; individual trials last minutes

D3_recording_days.evidence: Mice were trained over two days (trials 1-6). Drugs were administered on day 3 before trial 7

D4_baseline.evidence: Two-way repeated measures ANOVA were performed with data from both sexes and trials 6-9 ... time differences between trials 6 and 7 to quantify drug effects on overnight recall

D5_followup.evidence: All post-drug trials (7-9) on day 3 within ~2 h of injection

judge_notes: Four behavioural assays retained (HTR, Open Field, Rotarod, Puzzle Box); plasma corticosterone (HPA axis) and PFC EEG excluded as physiological/neural endpoints per rubric — all candidates agreed.

B1 for HTR, OFT and Rotarod set to 0 (single measure); gemma's score of 1 for a single measure was inconsistent with the rubric point mapping. Puzzle box B1 = 2 (4 measures: latency + three derived recall/problem-solving scores); gemma's score of 4 corrected to 2.

Rotarod B2 overridden to 0: latency was measured in separate trials at intervals after injection (scored as multiple discrete sessions in D1 by all candidates), which is between-trial, not within-session dynamics.
HTR D2 set to 1 (30 min falls in 15–60 min); gemma's <15 min was an error.

OFT D4 set to 0: the pre-psychedelic 30-min exploration followed saline/MDL injection and its data were not reported. OFT setup_habituation = yes (modal), based on the 30-min apparatus exposure before the second injection.
Puzzle box setup_habituation set to not_reported: trials 1-6 are data-collecting training trials (trial 6 used in analysis), not a no-data habituation per rubric.

Puzzle box time_to_assay set to acute_0to2h (15 min LSD, 60 min lisuride, all within 2 h) rather than 'multiple', since the rubric reserves 'multiple' for the same assay at distinct timepoints such as 30 min vs 24 h.
Rotarod n reconstructed as 6 drug conditions (including MDL+saline, n = 5/sex) × 2 sexes × 5 minus one MDL+LSD male = 59; OFT n summed from text (132) including MDL+saline.
LSD 1 mg/kg excluded from dosing because it was used only in the EEG experiment; MDL 100907 (0.5 mg/kg i.p.) added as a dosing entry since it was administered in the behavioural experiments.
day_night_flipped = no (modal), based on explicit statement that testing occurred during the light phase.
